title: Interview candidate: Samuel (@samuel.fm), who updated a browser flight game every day of the window and answered the people playing it
summary: Samuel (54,200 followers) posted updates to a flight combat game at flight.mozzius.dev on four days of the window: new terrain, weather and a challenge mode (13 Nov), multiplayer ("dogfight your mutuals!", 13 Nov, 187 likes), difficulty settings and a leaderboard (13 Nov), matchmaking (14 Nov), a tutorial (14 Nov), two more maps (15 Nov) and three new aircraft (18 Nov). Under those posts people asked how it works, how to play and whether he could add things, and several of the things asked for appear in the next update: a player said the enemies were shooting at them and difficulty settings came about four hours later; a member asked for a lobby and matchmaking and matchmaking came the next morning; someone asked for a tutorial and it came seven and a half hours later. The card lists 11 of his replies with the post each one answered.

candidate.source: Found by the researcher in posts.jsonl; he is not in the digest's Interview material. By my own count with a similar rule he has 15 question-and-answer pairs from 15 askers, most of them under his own posts about the game.

checks.optOutList: not on the opt-out list (packages/scraper/config/optout.json, loaded through the tool)
checks.bio: not checked: the digest carries no bios and research has no network. The scraper reports that it excluded accounts with profile opt-outs before the digest was written.
checks.windowPosts: Read his 16 top-level posts and all of his replies to other people's questions that the data holds (16, of which 1 is in a flagged story). One of his top-level posts is in a flagged story (a one-line post about a pope, flagged identity). Some of his replies are about bugs in the Bluesky app and read as coming from someone who works on it; those are left off. No post asks not to be quoted.

didInWindow: Built and kept updating flight.mozzius.dev, a flight combat game in the browser with desktop builds on GitHub. In his words it was "vibe coded" ("yep! been a blast, I've wanted this to exist for so long and now it does"). Multiplayer signs in with a Bluesky account and, per his reply, relays each client's position over a websocket 20 times a second. He posted his own high score, then congratulated another account that beat it (18 Nov).
couldBeShown: flight.mozzius.dev is a public page; the researcher has not opened it.
The multiplayer post has an image. Alt text: "my flight sim game on a laptop and a phone. on the laptop a missile is streaking towards mozzius.dev. on the phone a missile warning is visible".
The other update posts have screenshots, and the 18 Nov follow-up has a video; no alt text for those in the data.
The sequence of dated update posts, each listing what was added, is itself on the card as context.

notUnderstood: I have not played the game or seen its screenshots. "Ace Combat" is a published series of flight combat games. "HOTAS" is a kind of flight stick. "railway" in the "how-multiplayer" answer is a hosting service, as I read it.
leftOut: His replies about bugs in the Bluesky app and to people asking him to look into them (these touch his job). A reply to someone asking why they were shadowbanned. A reply about an agent refusing a login flow. An exchange about adding "the warthog" whose image I have not seen, followed by a joke about lawyers. A post about a pope (flagged).
sensitive: At 54,200 followers he is one of the eight members above 20,000 that the scope review points to: he came in on the follow rule, and an interview subject is not meant to be picked for follower count. Members did play the game and ask him things, which is why he is here. Several of his other replies in the window are about his work on the Bluesky app; his employer and job are offline life (R1) and are not on the card. The game is about aerial combat (missiles, "bandits", named military aircraft): fiction, but worth a glance from the screen. The prompt in the "shooting" pair carries a "grief and disaster" keyword mark in the data; the post is about being shot at in the game, and I included it because the answer and the update that followed depend on it. Two askers are small accounts and appear only as people whose requests he met.
